author: Andrew Fisher

checks.name: only the helper and exact sample selection changed
allocation, incomplete-target cleanup, disposal and resolve remain byte-identical
all 1024 colour/depth/request combinations satisfy the bounded rule
2x stays 2x when both support it
4x fallback requires both actual attachment formats
8x alone cannot satisfy the bounded 2x fallback
ordinary 4x and higher requests keep the original maximum-at-or-below rule
missing capability lists return no multisampling
RGBA8 chooses 4x for colour and matching depth
RGBA8 success allocates exactly the existing three MSAA objects
RGBA8 resolves colour and depth with existing nearest blit
RGBA8 disposal releases all target and MSAA objects
RGBA8 incomplete allocation restores 1x and deletes all partial MSAA objects
RGBA8 failed allocation never attempts resolve
RGBA8 failed-allocation teardown leaves no objects
HDR chooses 4x for colour and matching depth
HDR success allocates exactly the existing three MSAA objects
HDR resolves colour and depth with existing nearest blit
HDR disposal releases all target and MSAA objects
HDR incomplete allocation restores 1x and deletes all partial MSAA objects
HDR failed allocation never attempts resolve
HDR failed-allocation teardown leaves no objects
0 requested keeps the original early no-allocation path
1 requested keeps the original early no-allocation path
incompatible attachment capabilities allocate nothing
successive quality target replacement leaks no framebuffer or renderbuffer

limits: CPU mocked capability/allocation lifecycle; real GL validation remains required.
Counts are attachment storage estimates; driver allocation padding and real-device timing are not measured.
Incomplete-framebuffer failure path is preserved; no new exception or out-of-memory recovery mechanism is introduced.
